survey: A black cast-iron cauldron shown in three-quarter view from slightly above, sitting on a purple stone-tile floor. Main parts: (1) A round, bulging pot body with a thick rolled rim. Its opening faces up and toward the camera, and it is filled to the rim with bubbling green liquid. (2) Two side handles. The left one is a closed loop that comes out of a small tab just under the rim. The right one is a ring hanging from a rectangular lug set lower on the body, at the shoulder. (3) Short stubby legs with flared feet resting flat on the tiles. One is visible front-left and one back-right; a third is probably hidden behind the fire, which is plausible for a tripod. (4) A small fire of crossed sticks on the floor under the pot, in the gap between the pot bottom and the floor. The legs touch the floor, the body sits on the legs, the liquid sits inside the rim, and the fire sits under the pot.

errors.where: The two side handles (left upper side vs right shoulder)
errors.what: Parts that should mirror each other differ. The left handle is a plain loop on a small tab right under the rim. The right handle is a ring hanging from a large rectangular lug much lower on the body. A real cauldron has two matching handles at the same height, so the pot would hang crooked from a bail.

fix: Cast-iron cauldron with two identical, symmetrical side handles: each is a matching ring hanging from a small rectangular lug, both at the same height just below the rim, placed on opposite sides of the pot.
